title: Overload threshold tuning sheet (Hosted API) — baselines + proposed breaker thresholds
body:
README / HOW TO USE
- Purpose: track observed baseline saturation + propose circuit breaker / load-shedding thresholds per region + model.
- Applies to Hosted API request path (gateway admission + routing + runtime backpressure). Dedicated/Private are out-of-scope except where noted.
- Signals referenced here match runtime export work (queue depth, token/sec saturation, KV cache pressure proxy, HBM free%).
- IMPORTANT: thresholds are starting points. Expect 2–3 tuning passes once canary + perf-canary burst scenarios are stable.

Definitions (shorthand used in tables)
- prefill_q_p95: p95 prefill queue depth (requests waiting at runtime) during steady-state load.
- decode_q_p95: p95 decode queue depth during steady-state load.
- sched_backlog_ms_p95: p95 scheduler backlog in ms (runtime admission -> start token).
- tps_sat_p95: p95 token/sec saturation ratio (1.0 == fully saturated decode loop; >1 indicates sustained saturation / debt).
- kv_press_p95: p95 KV cache pressure proxy (0–1). Higher == more eviction/thrash risk.
- hbm_free_p05: p05 HBM free % (lower tail is what hurts us).
- shed_soft: start shedding / degrading under duress (feature reductions, caps). Should be earlier than breaker_open.
- breaker_open: hard reject with overload error (customer-visible 429/503 per error taxonomy).
- breaker_close: close when recovered (hysteresis to avoid flapping).
- half_open_probe_rps: probe rate when transitioning from open -> half-open.
- retry_after_s: recommended Retry-After seconds for hard rejections (tier-aware).

Assumptions / global guardrails
- Goal: keep p99 latency stable under bursts and avoid timeouts/retry storms. Prefer early explicit overload over silent timeouts.
- Hysteresis: breaker_close is always meaningfully below breaker_open (typically 60–75% of open threshold).
- Cardinality guardrail: thresholds must not require per-tenant per-GPU tuning (we only do per region/model + tier overrides).
- Tier behavior (initial proposal):
  - Self-serve: more aggressive shed + shorter Retry-After.
  - Enterprise Hosted (SLA): shed first (degradation) and bias routing fallback if configured; still reject before timeouts.

================================================================================
TAB: Proposed thresholds (v0)
(Proposal owner: Aisha/Rafael; review with Runtime + Routing before canary widening)

Notes on columns
- All thresholds are evaluated on rolling windows (default 30s) with min-sample guards.
- We should prefer composite rules (e.g., backlog AND tps saturation) to avoid false positives from short spikes.
- For simplicity, each row expresses: shed_soft triggers first; breaker_open triggers hard reject; breaker_close defines recovery.

Follow-up from canary
- SUP-2860 reported missing Retry-After on some overload responses (fixed in rollout hotfix; verify headers at gateway + downstream).
- We need explicit dashboard panel that overlays breaker_open events with deploy markers (telemetry: Logan).

================================================================================
TAB: Notes / follow-ups
Open questions
1) Should hbm_free_p05 threshold be adjusted by hardware class (A100 vs H100 pools)? Right now we assume consistent pools per region/model.
2) Can we rely on kv_press_p95 as a stable proxy? Runtime team flagged sampling jitter at low traffic.
3) Error semantics: when do we emit 429 vs 503 for overload? Proposal: 429 when tenant-specific quota/concurrency cap; 503 when platform overload breaker.

Tuning playbook (quick)
- If breaker opens too late (timeouts still occur): lower breaker_open backlog threshold by 10–15% OR add composite condition with tps_sat.
- If breaker flaps: widen hysteresis (lower breaker_close), increase evaluation window (30s -> 60s), and increase min_samples.
- If shed_soft engages too aggressively: move shed_soft up (require 2 signals) and ensure shed actions are reversible.

Planned edits for v1 (target 2025-12-15)
- Add explicit min-sample gates (avoid false opens during metric dropouts).
- Add deploy suppression option for runtime rollouts (max 10m, only for self-serve).
- Add tier override for enterprise-hosted: try routing fallback once (bounded) before hard reject.

Last touchpoints
- 2025-12-06: Reviewed with Christine (overload protection eng) + Sofia (runtime scheduling). Agreed backlog thresholds look reasonable; kv pressure signal still under review.
- 2025-12-09: Rafael requested: add a row for ap-southeast llama-70b once capacity comes online; pending.
